daily_brief: Russian missile strikes killed at least eight people in Kyiv overnight, damaging residential buildings, a children's hospital, and a school in what Ukrainian officials described as a 'massive attack' [BBC, Al Jazeera, France 24]. The strikes came as former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov called for wartime elections, presenting the biggest political challenge to President Zelensky since the 2022 invasion [BBC]. In economic news, Evergrande founder Hui Ka Yan was sentenced to life in prison in China after pleading guilty to embezzlement and bribery, marking a decisive moment in the fallout from China's property crisis [BBC, Nikkei Asia, Financial Times]. President Trump escalated pressure on Iran, threatening 'tremendous economic consequences' on any country doing business with Tehran following the expiry of a 60-day ceasefire [BBC, Al Jazeera]. Meanwhile, Australia expressed outrage after Israel declined to open criminal proceedings over the 2024 killing of aid worker Zomi Frankcom in the World Central Kitchen strike, with Foreign Minister Penny Wong summoning the Israeli ambassador [BBC, Al Jazeera]. In Central African Republic, over 100 people died when an illegal goldmine collapsed near the Cameroon border [The Guardian, Le Monde].

top_stories.headline: Russian Missile Barrage Kills at Least Eight in Kyiv, Damages Children's Hospital
bullets: Overnight Russian missile strikes hit residential buildings, warehouses, a children's hospital, and a school in Kyiv, killing at least eight people and injuring 33
A nine-storey residential building collapsed and caught fire in Solomianskyi district; rescue crews pulled survivors from rubble
A Russian drone crossed into Romanian airspace near Galați, crashing in an uninhabited area with no casualties; Poland activated defensive air operations
Russia's defence ministry claimed strikes targeted drone production facilities, a military depot, and logistics hub

top_stories.headline: Evergrande Founder Hui Ka Yan Sentenced to Life in Prison as China Property Crisis Reaches Legal Conclusion
bullets: Hui Ka Yan, founder of collapsed property giant Evergrande, received life sentence and had all personal property confiscated after pleading guilty to embezzlement and corporate bribery
Shenzhen court fined Hui's former companies 15.82 billion yuan ($2.35 billion) for falsifying records and concealing debt
Other executives including Hui's two sons received sentences ranging from 22 months to 18 years
Once Asia's richest man, Hui rose from rural poverty to oversee Evergrande's aggressive expansion before its collapse shook China's property sector

top_stories.headline: Trump Threatens 'Economic D-Day' on Countries Doing Business with Iran
bullets: President Trump announced 'the most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country' targeting nations helping Iran, following expiry of 60-day ceasefire on Monday
Threat extends Operation Economic Fury launched in April to sanction foreign banks and firms doing business with Tehran
UAE announced it would sever all financial and economic ties with Iran one day before Trump's announcement
Trump cited oil smuggling, swap lines, cash transfers, and front companies but did not specify punishments or name targeted countries

top_stories.headline: Australia Summons Israeli Ambassador After IDF Declines Criminal Investigation into Aid Worker Deaths
bullets: Israel's military decided not to launch criminal investigation into April 2024 airstrike that killed Australian aid worker Zomi Frankcom and six World Central Kitchen colleagues
Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong called decision 'outrageous' and said it 'falls far short of the accountability we expect'
Israeli Ambassador Hillel Newman defended IDF, stating 'there was no criminal intention' and therefore 'no criminal responsibility'
Wong questioned why two additional strikes followed the first if it was a 'catastrophic error,' noted drone audio still not provided to Australia

top_stories.headline: Over 100 Dead After Illegal Goldmine Collapses in Central African Republic
bullets: Landslide caused collapse at artisanal goldmine in village of Zamboye, about 50km from Baboua near Cameroon border, on Tuesday afternoon
More than 100 bodies recovered according to Red Cross volunteers and local mining association officials
Victims believed to be nationals of Central African Republic and Cameroon; rescue operations ongoing to find survivors
Authorities launched investigation; collapse attributed to underground tunnel failure
